explanations.answer: He must be put to death
explanations.explanation: That's what the LORD says: “…who gives any of his children to Molech must be put to death.” (Leviticus 20:2) This is a heavy one, friend, so I'm not going to joke about it. The words are plain, and I'll leave them plain.

explanations.answer: He must pay a heavy fine
explanations.explanation: No money changes hands in this verse. The LORD says the man “must be put to death.” (Leviticus 20:2) A fine would be a much lighter thing than what the text says. This is a heavy part of the sermon, so we'll just let the LORD's words stand.

The verse doesn't mention any warnings, friend, not two and not one. It says the man “must be put to death.” (Leviticus 20:2) I could stretch the text to fit that answer, but I won't. The LORD's words are heavy enough as they are.

The LORD actually says “Any Israelite or foreigner living in Israel…” (Leviticus 20:2) That second group is easy to skip right past, but it's in the verse. So this law covers foreigners living in Israel too, not only Israelites.

Right, because the verse names both groups: “Any Israelite or foreigner living in Israel…” (Leviticus 20:2) It's a short little phrase, and it's easy to read right over it. Foreigners living in Israel are included in this law along with the Israelites.

That's the group the LORD names: “The people of the land are to stone him.” (Leviticus 20:2) Notice it isn't handed to one office or one small group. It's the people of the land. It's a heavy line, so I'll just keep to what the verse says.

The priests aren't named in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “The people of the land are to stone him.” (Leviticus 20:2) It's easy to picture priests handling serious business like this, because they do handle a lot in this book. But this verse names the people of the land.

Elders and gates don't show up in this verse. The LORD says, “The people of the land are to stone him.” (Leviticus 20:2) I know you can picture a group of elders at a gate, but that picture isn't in this verse. The text gives this job to the people of the land.

explanations.answer: It defiles His sanctuary and profanes His holy name
explanations.explanation: The LORD gives His reason in His own words: “…he has defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name.” (Leviticus 20:3) The reason is right there in the verse, so we don't have to guess at one. Giving his offspring to Molech touched the LORD's sanctuary and His holy name.

explanations.answer: It breaks a promise the people made to Moses
explanations.explanation: No promise to Moses, Israel's leader, shows up in this verse. The reason the LORD gives is that “…by giving his offspring to Molech, he has defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name.” (Leviticus 20:3) The LORD names two things that were touched, His sanctuary and His holy name. I'd stick with the reason He actually gives.

explanations.answer: It brings war and trouble on the whole land
explanations.explanation: The verse doesn't say a word about war, friend. The LORD says the man “…has defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name.” (Leviticus 20:3) That's the reason in the text, and I'm not going to add one. The sanctuary and the holy name are what the LORD names.

Close, but that's not the word in the verse. The LORD says He will set His face “…against that man and his family…” (Leviticus 20:5) Neighbors aren't named there. The word in the blank is family.
